_comment: Desired GitHub configuration for joaodinissf's personal repositories. Applied by ./apply.sh, which is idempotent: re-running is a no-op when reality already matches. Run without --apply to see drift.
_scope: Scope is discovered, not listed. Every public, non-fork, non-archived repo owned by the authenticated user is governed by the defaults below. This file holds the policy and the exceptions to it, never the inventory, so a repo created tomorrow is covered without editing anything. Private repos are out of scope.

defaults._private_note: Private repos get merge settings and nothing else -- no rulesets, no secret scanning, both of which need paid features there. Auto-merge is off because it requires branch protection, which is exactly what cannot be created. Their coverage exists so that nothing is lost from the standardize-repo-settings gist this repo replaces.
defaults._security_note: Every key under security is sent verbatim as a flag, so no annotation can live inside it. secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns and secret_scanning_validity_checks are deliberately absent: they require Advanced Security, and without it GitHub accepts the PATCH with 200 and silently ignores it. Declaring them would report drift on every repo forever, costing this file its exit-0 drift check. Add them if the account ever gains Secret Protection.

branch_ruleset._note: zero approvals, because these are single-author repos: the rule to enforce is that every change arrives as a pull request, not that someone else signs it off. No required_status_checks either -- most of these repos have no CI, and a required check that never reports blocks the branch permanently.

defaults._tag_note: release tags are immutable; anything else is not. Three patterns because three naming conventions are in use -- bare (v1.0), component-prefixed (jdf-tab-huddle-v0.2.2) and namespaced (release/1.0). Names outside them, such as nightly or latest, stay movable, which is what removes any reason to disable the ruleset by hand. Creation is deliberately not blocked: the property worth having is that a published tag never moves, and blocking creation would mean no release could be tagged without a bypass actor -- and a bypass actor makes the whole ruleset advisory for whoever holds it.

_exception_shape.name: required -- the repo this entry applies to
_exception_shape.topics: optional -- reconciled only where declared, because a default of [] would strip topics off every repo that has any
_exception_shape.branch_ruleset: optional -- an object overriding ref_include / required_approving_review_count / required_review_thread_resolution / required_status_checks, or null to exempt the repo (an empty repo has no branches, so no ruleset can be created)
_exception_shape.tag_ruleset: optional -- false to skip tag protection
_exception_shape.tag_ref_include: optional -- overrides the default tag patterns
